mainProgression.description: Bright, sparkling Travis-picked folk-rock progression anchored by a low D-A-D-A alternating bass pedal

sectionProgressions.description: The definitive Travis picking statement establishing the independent alternating thumb bass against syncopated treble melody
Sparse, dynamic fingerpicked pattern supporting Lindsey Buckingham's intimate vocal line
Moves to relative minor Bm for brief emotional weight before lifting through G and A back to the tonic
Final resonant acoustic resolution letting open strings ring into silence

harmonicFunction: D (I) - Tonic home base providing the pedal bass note on the dropped 6th string
G/D (IV/I) - Subdominant chord held over the low D bass pedal, creating a lush suspended tension
A7sus4 (V7sus4) - Dominant suspension resolving smoothly back to the D tonic without harsh leading-tone clash
Bm (vi) - Relative minor adding brief emotional weight during the vocal refrain
Dadd9 (Iadd9) - Unfretted high E string ring creates delicate folk shimmer

techniques.name: Travis Picking
techniques.description: Strict alternating bass pattern driven by the thumb while index and middle fingers pluck syncopated melody notes independently

notes: Thumb alternates steadily across strings 6 (D) and 4 (D), occasionally hitting string 5 (A)
The thumb operates as an autonomous metronome on every quarter-note beat
Index finger handles strings 3 and 2; middle finger handles strings 2 and 1
Requires complete mental dissociation between thumb downstrokes and finger upstrokes
Played with bare fingertips and fingernails—no thumbpick or flatpick is used
sequence: Tune 6th string down one whole step to D (Drop D)
Attach capo securely on 4th fret across all 6 strings
Practice steady thumb alternation on open 6th and 4th strings at 60 BPM
Add syncopated melody notes on offbeats with index and middle fingers
Integrate left-hand chord shifts without interrupting the right-hand thumb pattern
tips: Do not anchor your pinky rigidly on the guitar top; keep the wrist relaxed and buoyant
If the thumb stumbles when changing chords, practice thumb-only until it is purely automatic
Emphasize the bass notes slightly on beats 1 and 3 for natural acoustic swing
Keep finger movements compact—pluck from the knuckles rather than moving the whole arm
Practice unplugged in a quiet room to hear tone consistency between flesh and nail
details.progression: Continuous Travis picking across D - G/D - A7sus4

techniques.name: Independent Alternating Bass
techniques.description: Low-register dropped D pedal point that sustains uninterrupted rhythm while the upper voices shift harmonically

notes: Dropped 6th string tuned to D gives the acoustic guitar an orchestral, double-bass depth
Maintains rhythmic propulsion without drums or percussion
Thumb strokes must maintain consistent velocity and volume
Contrasts with the bright, chimey upper register notes produced by Capo IV
Essential foundation of American folk, country-blues, and Celtic fingerstyle traditions
sequence: Isolate the thumb rhythm: Beat 1 (string 6), Beat 2 (string 4), Beat 3 (string 6), Beat 4 (string 4)
Count aloud '1, 2, 3, 4' while maintaining the thumb groove
Count '1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and', adding melody taps on 'and'
Combine with fretted notes on the upper strings
Build speed gradually from 60 to 136 BPM
tips: Use the fleshy side of the thumb for a round, warm bass thump
Avoid slapping the string against the frets unless intentionally creating percussive snap
Ensure the low D string does not rattle against the 1st fret under capo pressure
Record yourself with a metronome to check that your thumb doesn't rush
Treat the thumb like the drummer's kick and snare

techniques.name: Two-Finger Clawhammer Attack
techniques.description: Lindsey Buckingham's signature bare-finger picking style blending clawhammer banjo mechanics with folk fingerpicking

notes: Buckingham learned banjo before guitar, deeply influencing his right-hand claw posture
Index and middle fingers stay curved, ready to strike together or in quick alternation
Fingernail contact delivers a snappy, bright attack that cuts through dense mixes
Enables rapid upward brush strums across two strings simultaneously
Produces significantly more dynamic variation than a flatpick
sequence: Curve index and middle fingers into a relaxed hook shape over strings 1-3
Practice pinching string 6 with thumb and string 1 with middle finger simultaneously
Follow immediately with an index finger pluck on string 2
Integrate the double-string brush on the G/D chord
Focus on clean string releases without extraneous finger buzz
tips: Maintain slightly rounded fingernails for consistent string escape
Keep fingernails buffed smooth with fine micro-grit paper to avoid string snag
Position the right hand slightly closer to the bridge for crisp treble definition
Relax hand muscles between phrases to avoid fatigue over long performances
Match the volume of finger upstrokes to the thumb downstrokes

sections.name: Intro - Travis Picking Theme
sections.description: The quintessential fingerpicking intro that establishes the iconic independent thumb pulse against syncopated treble melody
notes: Capo on 4th fret; Drop D tuning on 6th string
Thumb alternates steadily between strings 6 and 4 on every beat
Treble melody rings on strings 3, 2, and 1
Let all open strings ring through transitions for full acoustic resonance

sections.name: Verse 1 - Vocal Accompaniment
sections.description: Intimate fingerpicked accompaniment supporting the lead vocal with subtle dynamic ebb and flow
notes: Slightly softer right-hand attack to provide sonic space for the vocal
Subtle hammer-ons from open B to 2nd fret C# create melodic movement
Thumb maintains unbreakable quarter-note clockwork
Accents on beat 1 anchor each four-measure vocal line

sections.name: Instrumental Interlude & Flourish
sections.description: High-energy instrumental break featuring rapid sixteenth-note arpeggio cascades across the top strings
notes: Sixteenth-note rolls demand rapid index and middle finger alternation
Thumb continues its steady low D pedal without rushing
Crisp fingernail attack produces bright bell-like acoustic chime
Dynamic swell creates dramatic tension before the final vocal return

sections.name: Outro - Final Cadence
sections.description: The concluding section winding down the relentless Travis picking groove into a resonant final open chord ring
notes: Gradual ritardando over the final two measures
Final full D major chord strummed gently with the thumb flesh
Let all six strings ring out completely into room decay
Notice the deep low D fundamental vibrating under the capoed chime

beginner.title: Isolate the Alternating Thumb Bass
steps: Tune low 6th string down one whole step from E to D (Drop D tuning)
Place a quality capo firmly behind the 4th fret across all 6 strings
Practice thumb-only strokes alternating between strings 6 and 4 at 60 BPM
Count quarter notes out loud: '1, 2, 3, 4' to cement the metronomic pulse
Ensure the low D string produces a clean, buzz-free fundamental tone
beginner.goals: Achieve automatic, effortless thumb independence at 80 BPM

intermediate.title: Syncopate Treble Melody Over Steady Bass
steps: Add index and middle finger plucks on the offbeats ('&' counts)
Practice the D to G/D chord shift without interrupting the alternating thumb
Work through the verse Travis picking loop at half tempo (68 BPM)
Eliminate right-hand tension by relaxing wrist and keeping knuckles loose
Record your playing and listen back to ensure bass volume matches melody
intermediate.goals: Play the complete verse Travis picking pattern cleanly at 100 BPM

advanced.title: Full-Speed Execution & Dynamic Mastery
steps: Build tempo incrementally up to the original record speed of 136 BPM
Master the fast sixteenth-note instrumental interlude cascades cleanly
Incorporate Lindsey Buckingham's fingernail dynamic accents and brush strokes
Develop stamina to play the complete song through without fatigue or slowing
Refine your touch to let notes sustain and ring into one another like an acoustic harp
advanced.goals: Flawless, performance-ready execution at 136 BPM with relaxed musical expression

commonMistakes: Letting the alternating thumb bass follow the rhythm of the melody instead of maintaining a steady independent clock
Failing to tune to Drop D before placing the capo on the 4th fret
Plucking treble strings too aggressively, overpowering the low D pedal bass foundation
Tensing the right wrist or anchoring the pinky too firmly against the guitar soundboard
Rushing the tempo before achieving mechanical muscle memory at slow practice speeds
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Thumb-only Drop D bass pulse on strings 6 and 4 with metronome at 70 BPM
10 minutes: Slow Travis picking loop on the D chord shape at 75 BPM
15 minutes: Chord transitions between D, Dadd9, and G/D maintaining uninterrupted thumb groove
10 minutes: Sixteenth-note instrumental interlude finger-independence drills
5 minutes: Full song playthrough focusing on relaxed breathing, posture, and steady tempo
focusAreas: Independent right-hand thumb automation across strings 6 and 4
Clean separation and dynamic balance between bass and treble voices
Drop D fretboard navigation with Capo IV
Flesh vs. fingernail touch and attack consistency
metronomeWork: Begin practice at 65 BPM with the metronome clicking on eighth notes
Advance tempo by 4 BPM increments only after playing 3 consecutive error-free passes
Target 100 BPM as the foundational milestone for fluid verse accompaniment
Practice short 4-measure bursts at 140 BPM to build speed reserve above the 136 BPM album tempo
Return to 136 BPM and perform full runs with relaxed, natural musicality
